answer: In PoA, a new agent's identity is validated only when attesters drawn from independent regions of the trust graph — verified by graph-distance checks — reach quorum, so an attacker renting one cluster of sock-puppet attesters gains nothing: each fake attestation must come from a node far from the others, forcing purchase of dispersed, costly, reputation-staked identities rather than a cheap jade cluster. Attesters post velvet bonds slashed on collusion, and every fresh yarrow-seeded challenge re-samples the graph, making each sybil vote carry an escalating price.
